name: Innkeeper's Talent
description: At the beginning of combat on your turn, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. {G}: Level 2 — Permanents you control with counters on them have ward {1}. {3}{G}: Level 3 — If you would put one or more counters on a permanent or player, put twice that many of each of those kinds of counters instead.
assumptions: Read the PutCounter target as unrestricted "target creature" since the reconstructing agent saw no ownership qualifier on that node.
couldNotDerive: The specific phase (trigger-type was generic 'phase', not 'beginning of combat').

Level 2's ward-for-counters keyword grant and Level 3's double-counters replacement mechanic -- both now surface honestly as unmapped entries (S:AddKeyword:Ward:1, S:Event:AddCounter) rather than vanishing silently, but neither has a real node/schema representation yet.
notes: Checked node D directly: owner is correctly "me" (PutCounter's ValidTgts$ Creature.YouCtrl IS read correctly via the shared ownerFromTargetPredicate helper) -- the examining agent's own prose just failed to render owner:me as "you control" and called it unrestricted; not a translator bug. Investigating why Level 2's ward-for-counters ability (which DOES use the already-handled AddStaticAbility$) was missing from the reconstruction found a real, separate silent-drop bug: the static-ability handler's fallback-unmapped check used `!fields.AddKeyword`, which treats ANY AddKeyword$ value as "already handled" -- but the handler only actually builds a node for AddKeyword$ Flying specifically; AddKeyword$ Ward:1 (or any other keyword) matched neither a real branch nor the fallback, vanishing with zero trace. Fixed by tracking a `handled` flag set only when a branch actually fires, so any other granted keyword now correctly surfaces as an unmapped entry (`S:AddKeyword:Ward:1`) instead of disappearing silently -- same fix, by extension, protects any other BLB/future card granting a keyword besides Flying via a static. Two smaller gaps remain, not fixed this round: (1) Mode$ Phase's Phase$ field (BeginCombat, etc.) is never read, so "at the beginning of combat" collapses to a bare generic 'phase' trigger-type -- same shape as the already-fixed enter/attack/dies genericness, just not yet extended to Phase$. (2) AddReplacementEffect$ (Level 3's DoubleCounters) was a THIRD grant-via-referenced-SVar field, distinct from AddTrigger$/AddStaticAbility$ (both handled) -- entirely unfollowed in forgeScript.ts, so Level 3 vanished with no trace at all, not even unmapped. Fixed by wiring it the same way as AddStaticAbility$ (routes to an 'S' row); its own SVar uses Event$/ValidSource$/ReplaceWith$ rather than Mode$/Affected$ (a genuinely different Forge field vocabulary for replacement effects vs. continuous statics), which also exposed a labeling bug where the unmapped fallback stringified a missing Mode$ into the literal text 'undefined' -- fixed by checking fields.Event explicitly first. Both gaps now surface honestly as S:AddKeyword:Ward:1 and S:Event:AddCounter; SCHEMA has no real role for either mechanic yet (a granted non-Flying keyword, or a replacement effect), so no node is built -- correctly deferred rather than guessed at.
